messages:
sam: Planning KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC) — want a clear, auditable design for control-plane vs data-plane encryption. Separate CMKs? rotation + rewrap plan?
maria: +1 on separation. Control-plane (configs, metadata) uses Redwood-managed CMK in our account. Data-plane (customer blobs) should support customer-owned CMKs (cross-account) OR allow Redwood-managed per-tenant CMKs.
jon: If we accept customer CMKs we need a robust cross-account key policy and grant flow. Customers should give our service principal GenerateDataKey/Decrypt. Example key policy snippet we can ask customers to apply: ```{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodService",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDDWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-kms-access"},
      "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:ReEncrypt*"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}```
dima: We should always use envelope encryption: call KMS GenerateDataKey to get a plaintext DEK and a ciphertext DEK. Use local AES-GCM for payload encryption, store ciphertext DEK with object metadata. Never persist plaintext DEK. Cache DEKs in-memory per process with TTL (~5m) to reduce KMS QPS.
ellen: Audit reqs: CloudTrail must record all kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt, kms:ReEncrypt. Deliver trails to locked S3 bucket + push to SIEM. Retention: 1 year searchable for SOC2.
kms-bot: KMS health check: account/redwood-main CMK rotation enabled, cloudtrail pipeline healthy (last delivery 2026-01-12T03:12Z).
maria: Rotation policy: Redwood-managed CMKs we enable automatic rotation. For customer-managed keys we can't rotate on their behalf — they manage rotation. Need a rewrap strategy when CMK rotates (or if we change default CMK).
jon: Rewrap pattern: use AWS KMS ReEncrypt API to re-encrypt stored ciphertext DEKs from old CMK -> new CMK. Two options: eager backfill job to rewrap all objects, or lazy rewrap on first read/write. Lazy is lower immediate cost but leaves legacy-encrypted items until accessed. Track per-object metadata: `kms_key_arn` + `kms_key_version` to detect rewrap need.
dima: Note on grants: creating grants for high-throughput services avoids repeated KMS policy checks. Grants are tied to CMK and have a lifetime; when rotating CMK, grants become invalid. Also watch for grant leakage and implement grant revocation via RetireGrant where necessary.
ellen: Compliance checklist addition: record which principal performed decrypt (role/user), customer identifier, object id, operation, and KMS key used. That needs to be queryable for audit evidence.
sam: Performance/streaming concern: inference path cannot call KMS per token. Use session-level DEK (GenerateDataKey once per session) and encrypt streaming frames with local AEAD. Consider client-side chunking and DEK rotation per session.
maria: Also evaluate AWS XKS (external key store) and bring-your-own-key via ExternalKeyStore for customers requiring HSM-backed keys. Document differences and prod support matrix.
jon: Small IAM example for our service role permissions: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:ReEncrypt*"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:REGION:CUSTOMER_ACCOUNT:key/CUSTOMER_KEY_ID"
    }
  ]
}
```
dima: Security note: never log plaintext DEKs or un-encrypted payloads. Rotate service-level IAM keys regularly and use short-lived role assumptions (STS).
ellen: For evidence: add automated tests that show trail entries for a sample GenerateDataKey/Decrypt from a staging customer key. Capture logs in CI for audit sample.
sam: Next steps: draft operational runbook: key onboarding checklist (customer key policy snippet, granting role, test GenerateDataKey), rotation / rewrap runbook, CloudTrail + SIEM pipeline, monitoring alerts for KMS errors (Throttling/AccessDenied). I'll post a PR for the design doc tomorrow. :thumbsup:
jon: I'll add grant management helper and lazy rewrap worker prototype.
maria: I'll prepare the compliance matrix and example terraform module customers can apply to share keys safely.
ellen: +1, please cc security-ops for sign-off when PR is ready.
kms-bot: Reminder: next scheduled CMK rotation for account/redwood-main is 2026-03-01.
